# Harness Summary

The harness shows moderate but inconsistent performance across three datasets, with eval accuracies ranging from 54–58% but training accuracy significantly lagging in the smallest dataset (32% on ds_alpha). The core issue is systematic confusion between semantically similar classification labels—failures cluster around selecting plausible but incorrect near-neighbors from the demonstration set, with model reasoning consistently generic ("Closest demonstrations suggest X") lacking differentiation. Notable pattern: training accuracy lags most severely on the smallest dataset despite identical architecture, suggesting the few-shot demonstrations alone may be insufficient for reliable classification. Memory context grows steadily through training, but label selection errors persist throughout evaluation, indicating the in-context examples are neither well-stratified for the input domain nor producing robust learned prototypes. The larger datasets (beta, gamma) show more balanced train-eval splits, hinting that dataset scale partly masks the underlying confusion problem.
